newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Kashmir begins last stage of local polls.
newsitem.headline: India's Kashmir begins last stage of local polls.

text.p: Voting began on Monday in the troubled northern Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir in the last stage of local polls, officials said.
"There are not many people (voting) at the moment, but we expect the pace to pick up during the day," said one election official at Banihal, 95 km (55 miles) south of Srinagar.
An estimated 300,000 people are eligible to vote in the last part of polls to elect six representatives from the state's Doda district.

More than 20,000 paramilitary troops were guarding polling booths, residents said. At least 21 people, many of them political activists, died in violence accompanying the first three rounds of polling earlier this month.

The polls are the first to the state's 87-member assembly since 1987. New Delhi has ruled the Himalayan region directly since a separatist revolt broke out in 1990. More than 20,000 people have died since then, police and hospitals say.

India hopes the polls will be the first step on the road to restoring normalcy in the region. The three earlier phases saw an average estimated turn-out of about 55 percent of voters, government spokesman K.B. Jandial said.
